status_summary: DOT and NHTSA announced an AV Framework on 2025-04-24 and have since acted on parts of the NHTSA recommendation but not on the Standing General Order reversal. NHTSA streamlined crash reporting under the order, extended its exemption program to U.S.-built vehicles, proposed amendments to FMVSS Nos. 102, 103, 104, 110 and 135 for vehicles without manual controls (March to June 2026), withdrew the AV STEP proposal on 2026-06-26, and on 2026-07-31 granted Zoox a temporary exemption to deploy an ADS-equipped vehicle commercially. The Standing General Order remains in force and NHTSA says it is developing a rule to codify it, which differs from the Mandate's call to reverse it; a Federal Register query found no final rule on automated driving systems since August 2026. In Congress the SELF DRIVE Act (H.R. 7390) was forwarded by a House subcommittee on 2026-02-10 and has shown no later action; for trucking, no FMCSA rulemaking was found, only a pending Aurora exemption application.

timeline.event: DOT and NHTSA announce an automated vehicle framework (DOT press release of this date): crash reporting continues in streamlined form and the exemption program is extended to U.S.-built vehicles. NHTSA's 2026-07-31 notice (last entry) describes three goals for the framework (safe ongoing operations, removing unnecessary regulatory barriers and enabling commercial deployment) and a third amended Standing General Order issued the same day, which streamlines crash reporting for ADS and Level 2 ADAS (effective June 2025): severe crashes reported within five days, less severe ones monthly, duplicate reports and monthly zero reports removed.

House Energy and Commerce subcommittee forwards the SELF DRIVE Act of 2026 (H.R. 7390, introduced 2026-02-05), which would set federal automated vehicle safety standards and preempt state rules, to the full committee by a 12 to 11 roll call; no later action was found.
timeline.source: House Energy and Commerce Committee Republicans

timeline.event: NHTSA proposes to amend FMVSS No. 102 (and, in a companion proposal, Nos. 103 and 104) so ADS-equipped vehicles with no manual driving controls are not required to display transmission shift positions, saying this reduces compliance burden without affecting safety; comments closed 2026-04-15. NHTSA describes this as one of several rulemakings for ADS-equipped vehicles.

FMCSA publishes Aurora Operations' application for a five-year exemption allowing Level 4 ADS trucks to use cab-mounted flashing amber beacons instead of warning triangles or fusees; Aurora currently operates under a limited waiver that expires 2026-07-09. FMCSA had not decided the application, and 402 comments were received.

NHTSA submits to OMB a three-year reinstatement of the information collection behind Standing General Order 2021-01 (crash reporting for ADS and Level 2 ADAS), estimating 19,208 burden hours a year versus 31,319 under the prior approval; the order itself continues.

NHTSA withdraws the AV STEP proposed rule (a voluntary safety-reporting program proposed 2025-01-15), citing low expected participation and criticism from both industry and safety groups, and noting that exemption streamlining and SGO changes under the AV Framework serve similar goals. The same day it proposes updating FMVSS No. 135 for ADS-equipped vehicles.
NHTSA proposes to modernize FMVSS No. 135 (brake systems) to accommodate vehicles with automated driving systems.

NHTSA publishes AV Framework updates and interim guidance on commercial deployment exemptions under 49 CFR part 555. It reports that the AV Exemption Program now covers U.S.-built vehicles, that a rule to codify the Standing General Order is in development, that proposed rules would update FMVSS Nos. 102, 103, 104, 110 and 135, and that a rulemaking on ADS performance requirements was announced in March 2026; the comment period was later extended (notice of 2026-08-31).

NHTSA grants Zoox a two-year temporary exemption (49 CFR part 555; 91 FR 48494) from parts of eight FMVSS (Nos. 103, 104, 108, 111, 135, 201, 205, 208) to commercially deploy its ADS-equipped vehicle, through 2028-07-31 and up to 2,500 vehicles per 12 months; NHTSA describes it as the first passenger-carrying ADS vehicle exempted under its general exemption authority.
NHTSA extends the comment period on its AV Framework interim guidance to 2026-09-30 at the request of an industry association.

The H.R. 7390 status comes from a committee press page and a bill tracker (congress.gov could not be fetched).
